claim_ceiling: Language-dominated baseline embeddings do not support legally coherent fractal mapping. Two independent methods improve the legal/language purity ratio by ~20% (center-projection: +20%, Erwägungen TF-IDF: +10% legal purity) but no method achieves ratio >1.0. The fundamental challenge remains: the primary geometric signal in the BGer corpus is language, not legal content.
evidence_summary: Language debiasing cycle. Three approaches tested: (1) PCA language removal and center-projection — reduces language purity from 0.975 to 0.684 while maintaining legal purity at 0.295, achieving ratio 0.431 (+20% over baseline 0.359); (2) Citation-graph node2vec — limited by 5% coverage (50/1000 decisions), marginal improvement (ratio 0.380); (3) Reasoning-only TF-IDF on Erwägungen sections — achieves highest absolute legal purity (0.385, +10% over baseline 0.350). No method achieves target ratio >1.0. Hierarchy consistency maintained (NMI 0.86-0.90 for debiased vs 0.73-0.91 baseline). PCA2 and PCA3 produce identical results confirming language subspace is effectively 2-dimensional (DE vs FR). Scope violation diagnosed and repaired: researcher committed .opencode/agents/* changes (same class as prior runs 33020332703, 33020622379) — reverted. Critical bug fixed in citation_embeddings.py: node2vec library path now returns (matrix, vocab) tuple. All 10 new artifacts verified (shapes correct, file sizes match, JSON valid). All material quantitative claims independently confirmed against stored results. 49 evidence_refs all present on disk. Minor documentation issues: report table mixes sources without disclosure, NMI range rounded from 0.858-0.898 to 0.86-0.90, graph_only.npy stored as float64.
